Consumer complaint narrative: Subject : Improper Right of Offset, Failure to Close Personal Checking Account, and Continued Fees I am filing this complaint against Truist Bank regarding what I believe was an improper exercise of a Right of Offset against my personal checking account and the bank 's subsequent failure to close my account after my request. The overdraft resulted from a charge made by the corporation to XXXX. I dispute that I am personally liable for this corporate obligation and do not believe that I signed a personal guarantee making me personally responsible for the corporation 's business checking account overdraft. It is my understanding that the business account had been charged off and transferred or sold to a collection agency before Truist exercised the right of offset. My understanding is based on the fact that I have been contacted by XXXX different collection agencies, each attempting to collect this debt on behalf of Truist or its successor in interest. Because of these collection efforts, I believed the account was no longer being collected directly by Truist. If my understanding is correct and the debt had been transferred or sold before Truist debited my personal account, I question how Truist had the legal authority to exercise a right of offset after the debt had already been placed with third-party collectors. In addition, according to the collection agency currently attempting to collect this debt, the XXXX charge has never been paid and the debt remains outstanding. This raises serious concerns about how the {$650.00} withdrawn from my personal account was applied. If Truist took funds from my personal account to satisfy this obligation, I would expect the debt to have been credited accordingly. Instead, I have been informed that the XXXX charge remains unpaid. After Truist withdrew the {$650.00} from my personal account, I requested that my personal accounts be closed. Despite my request, Truist did not close the accounts and has continued to assess charges against them. I believe the bank failed to honor my request to close the accounts, resulting in additional charges that I should not have incurred. To date, Truist has not provided me with documentation establishing that it had the legal or contractual authority to withdraw funds from my personal checking account, explaining how the {$650.00} was applied, or explaining why my accounts were not closed when I requested. I respectfully request that the CFPB require Truist to provide : The specific contractual provision authorizing the right of offset against my personal checking account. Copies of any signed personal guarantee or other document establishing that I am personally liable for the corporation 's business checking account overdraft. Documentation showing whether Truist still owned the debt on the date the right of offset was exercised. The date the business overdraft was charged off. The date the debt was transferred or sold to any third party, if applicable. The names of the collection agencies to which the debt was assigned or transferred, and the dates of those assignments or transfers. A complete accounting showing exactly how the {$650.00} taken from my personal account was applied. An explanation of why the collection agency reports that the XXXX charge remains unpaid if Truist withdrew {$650.00} from my personal account to satisfy that obligation. An explanation of why Truist failed to close my personal accounts after I requested closure and why additional charges continued to be assessed. I respectfully request that Truist : Refund the {$650.00} if it can not demonstrate that it had the legal authority to exercise the right of offset against my personal account. Refund all fees and charges that were assessed after I requested that my personal accounts be closed. Refund all fees and charges that happened while I was trying to pay my car payment because of the offset. Provide written documentation supporting all actions taken on my accounts. Correct any records necessary to reflect the proper handling of this matter. I also request that the CFPB investigate whether Truist 's actions complied with applicable laws and regulations governing a bank 's right of offset, the collection of corporate debts, the handling of charged-off or transferred accounts, and its obligations when a customer requests that a deposit account be closed. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I appreciate your assistance in helping resolve this dispute. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, TN XXXX ( XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: FROM : XXXX XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX TO : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau | XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, IA XXXX DATE : XX/XX/XXXX RE : Formal Complaint Against NCB Management Services , Inc. for Violations of the FDCPA and FCRA ACCOUNT NO. XXXX XXXXXXXX I. INTRODUCTION AND STANDING I, XXXX, a consumer and resident of XXXX, Florida XXXX, hereby submit this formal written complaint against NCB Management Services , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA XXXX ) for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., concerning account number XXXX. I submit this complaint in my capacity as a federally protected consumer and respectfully request the full investigatory authority and remedial powers of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau be exercised in this matter. II. BACKGROUND AND FACTUAL BASIS OF DISPUTE On or about XX/XX/XXXX, the Respondent NCB Management Services , Inc. began reporting a debt to one or more consumer reporting agencies and/or attempted to collect an alleged debt that I expressly dispute as inaccurate, unverifiable, and/or not legally owed. Upon becoming aware of this collection activity and adverse reporting, I exercised my statutory rights by submitting a formal written request for debt validation on XX/XX/XXXX, via certified mail, with return receipt requested, directed to NCB Management Services , Inc. at its place of business. The Respondent failed to provide adequate validation of the alleged debt as required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g of the FDCPA. No documentation establishing the nature, amount, or legal basis of the alleged debt was provided within the applicable statutory period. Despite the absence of adequate validation and despite my express written dispute, the Respondent continued its collection and/or reporting activity. III. VIOLATIONS OF THE FAIR DEBT COLLECTION PRACTICES ACT ( FDCPA ) The Respondent 's conduct constitutes one or more violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. Specifically, the Respondent has engaged in the following unlawful acts and omissions : 1. Failure to Provide Debt Validation 15 U.S.C. 1692g : The Respondent failed to provide adequate written verification of the alleged debt within thirty ( 30 ) days of receiving my timely and properly submitted validation request dated XX/XX/XXXX. No documentation was furnished sufficient to establish the amount, origin, chain of ownership, or legal enforceability of the alleged debt associated with account XXXX. 2. Continued Collection Activity After Receipt of Validation Request 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) : Following receipt of my written dispute and validation request, the Respondent continued or failed to cease collection activity, including but not limited to continued adverse credit reporting. Such conduct is expressly prohibited under the FDCPA pending the provision of adequate debt validation. 3. Failure to Report Account as Disputed 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ) : The Respondent failed to communicate to the consumer reporting agencies that account XXXX was disputed by the consumer, or continued to report the alleged debt without disclosing the existence of my valid dispute. Reporting a debt while failing to note the consumer 's dispute constitutes a false, deceptive, or misleading representation in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ). 4. False, Deceptive, or Misleading Representations 15 U.S.C. 1692e : The Respondent used, or is believed to have used, false, deceptive, or misleading representations or means in connection with the collection of the alleged debt associated with account XXXX, in violation of the general prohibition set forth at 15 U.S.C. 1692e. This includes, but is not limited to, misrepresenting the character, amount, or legal status of the alleged debt. IV. VIOLATIONS OF THE FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT ( FCRA ) In addition to the foregoing FDCPA violations, the Respondent has violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., in its capacity as a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies. Specifically : 5. Furnishing Inaccurate Information FCRA 623 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) : The Respondent is furnishing or has furnished information regarding account xxxx1738 to one or more consumer reporting agencies that is inaccurate and/or can not be verified. As a furnisher of information, the Respondent bears an affirmative duty under FCRA 623 to report only accurate information and to promptly update or correct any information it knows or should know to be inaccurate. 6. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation FCRA 623 ( b ) : Upon receiving notice of my dispute whether directly or through a consumer reporting agency the Respondent failed to conduct a reasonable investigation into the accuracy of the reported information, in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). 7. Failure to Correct or Delete Inaccurate Information FCRA 623 ( b ) ( 1 ) ( E ) : Having received notice of my dispute, the Respondent has failed to correct, update, or arrange for the deletion of the inaccurate or unverifiable information associated with account XXXX from the relevant consumer reporting agency files, as required by law. V. RELIEF REQUESTED In light of the foregoing violations of federal consumer protection law, I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau take all appropriate action within its authority, including but not limited to the following specific relief : 8. Investigation : Conduct a full and thorough investigation into the Respondent 's conduct with respect to account XXXX and its compliance with the FDCPA and FCRA as described herein. 9. Deletion of Tradeline : Order NCB Management Services , Inc. to immediately and permanently delete the disputed tradeline associated with account XXXX from all consumer reporting agencies, including but not limited to XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 10. Cessation of Collection Activity : Order the Respondent to immediately cease all collection activity with respect to the alleged debt associated with account XXXX, including any direct or indirect contact, reporting, or referral to third parties. 11. Penalties and Remedies : Assess any and all appropriate civil penalties, fines, or remedies authorized by applicable law, including supervisory or enforcement actions consistent with the CFPB 's authority under the Consumer Financial Protection Act of XXXX ( 12 U.S.C. 5481 et seq. ). 12. Public Complaint Record : Maintain this formal complaint in the CFPB 's public Consumer Complaint Database as a matter of public record, and forward a copy to all relevant federal regulatory agencies as appropriate. VI. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND CLOSING STATEMENT Supporting documentation, including certified mail receipts evidencing the timely submission of my validation request dated XX/XX/XXXX, prior written correspondence with NCB Management Services , Inc., applicable credit report excerpts reflecting the disputed tradeline for account XXXX, and any other relevant records, is attached to this complaint and is available in full upon the CFPB 's request. I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the foregoing is true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief. I am a consumer protected under the FDCPA and FCRA, and I have a good-faith basis for each allegation set forth herein. I respectfully urge the Bureau to exercise the full extent of its investigatory and enforcement authority in this matter, and I stand ready to cooperate fully with any inquiry, provide additional documentation, or respond to any requests for information. I was never informed by GoodLeap of my rights under the FTC Holder Rule at the time of signing, nor was I advised of any consumer protections available to me if the contractor failed to perform. Resolution requested : I am requesting that the CFPB investigate GoodLeap 's practices in this matter and assist me in obtaining the following relief : Full cancellation of the {$31000.00} loan balance under the FTC Holder Rule Immediate deletion of the charge-off and all related derogatory reporting from my credit file at XXXX XXXX, and XXXX A written response from GoodLeap acknowledging my Holder Rule defenses Investigation into whether GoodLeap has engaged in a pattern of similar conduct with other consumers I have supporting documentation available including my original loan agreement, contractor contracts, correspondence showing non-completion of work, and my credit report showing the charge-off. Consumer complaint narrative: I am a confirmed successor in interest to a mortgage loan following my mothers death. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.36 ( i ), the servicer is required to promptly respond to requests for information and treat a confirmed successor in interest as a borrower for purposes of servicing. The servicer has failed to do so. Despite notifying the servicer of my status, they have refused to provide loan documentation, payment history, or other requested information, in violation of 12 C.F.R. 1024.36 and 1024.38 ( servicing policies and procedures ). I was never provided with any foreclosure notices, including Notice of Default or Notice of Trustee Sale. This raises serious concerns regarding compliance with 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( loss mitigation procedures ) and applicable notice requirements. I only became aware of the foreclosure when I contacted the servicer myself. After informing the servicer that I was actively attempting to sell the property, I was told that a third party had entered the property and was there to change the locks without my knowledge or consent. This action appears to be unlawful property interference, particularly as no confirmed foreclosure sale or lawful transfer of title had been communicated. Additionally, the servicer has failed to comply with obligations to maintain accurate information and provide continuity of contact under 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 and 1024.40. My probate attorney has issued a cease and desist letter. The servicer has ignored this and continues to withhold information and proceed without proper notice. These actions constitute potential violations of RESPA ( 12 U.S.C. 2605 ) and its implementing Regulation X, including but not limited to failures regarding successors in interest, requests for information, and foreclosure protections. I demand the following : 1. Immediate recognition of my status as a confirmed successor in interest. 2. Full loan documentation, including note, deed of trust, and complete payment history. 3. Proof of all foreclosure-related notices, including dates, addresses used, and method of delivery. 4. Confirmation of the current legal status of the property, including whether a foreclosure sale has occurred. 5. Immediate suspension of all foreclosure activity pending investigation of these violations. This matter involves potential wrongful foreclosure, failure of required notice, and unlawful interference with property rights, and requires urgent regulatory review.
